summary: NUP98 rearrangements or fusions are considered essential diagnostic criteria for acute myeloid leukemia with NUP98 rearrangement.

description:
IG::MYC fusions are detected in a subset of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL/LBL) cases. These fusions result from aberrant V(D)J recombination, most commonly involving IGH::MYC, and are associated with an immature B-cell phenotype. NRAS/KRAS mutations are frequently observed, while typical Burkitt lymphoma mutations are absent. The IGH::MYC fusion can co-occur with IGH::BCL2 in rare cases. Pediatric overlap cases may show mixed features of Burkitt-like morphology with precursor immunophenotype and KRAS/FBXO11 mutations.
Professional guidelines (WHO) list IG::MYC rearrangement as an essential diagnostic criteria for B-lymphoblastic leukemia with MYC rearrangement, classified under B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with other specified genetic abnormalities in WHO classification of tumors series (5th ed.; vol. 11).
name: AID166
summary: IG::MYC rearrangements or fusions are considered essential diagnostic criteria for B-lymphoblastic leukemia with MYC rearrangement, a subcategory of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with other defined genetic alterations in WHO classification.

description: The EPOR gene encodes the erythropoietin receptor, a member of the cytokine receptor family. EPOR rearrangements, including insertion of EPOR distal to the enhancer of either IGH or IGK or truncation of the cytoplasmic tail of EPOR result in abnormal EPOR activation and increased downstream JAK/STAT asignaling. These EPOR rearrangements are included in the set of genetic alterations sufficient for diagnosis of B-lymphoblastic leukaemia/lymphoma with BCR::ABL1-like features, an entity associated with a poor treatment response and high relapse rate which accounts for ~5-9% of B-ALL cases. JAK/STAT pathway activation offers Ruxolitinib (JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor) as a treatment option (AALL1521/INCB18424-269) COG AALL1521 phase II clinical trial).
name: AID167
summary: EPOR rearrangements are diagnostic for the BCR::ABL1-like subtype of B-lymphoblastic leukaemia/lymphoma

description: AML with inv(3)/t(3;3)(q21q26) is a distinct WHO-recognized entity. It is characterized by its aggressive course and poor prognosis. In this subtype of AML, translocation of GATA2 enhancer (located at 3q21) to MECOM (located at 3q26) leads to overexpression of the MECOM isoform EVI1 and monoallelic expression of GATA2, and lack of expression of full-length transcript MDS-EVI1. Besides the classical inv(3)/t(3;3)(q21q26) rearrangement, a number of atypical 3q26/MECOM rearrangements with poor treatment response in AML have been reported in literature. Since atypical 3q26 AMLs are difficult to diagnose given their cytogenetic complexity of and heterogeneity, the importance of routine molecular diagnosis to identify this subgroup of AML cases is highlighted. Use of MECOM FISH to identify 3q26/ MECOM rearrangements routinely for AML diagnostics, and quantitative EVI1 and MDS-EVI1 mRNA expression analysis are important to evaluate role of enhancer hijacking in EVI1 deregulation. It is proposed that both atypical 3q26/MECOM and inv(3)/t(3;3)(q21q26) be classified together as a single entity of 3q26 rearranged AMLs.

disease.name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With MECOM Rearrangement

name: AID168
summary: Approximately 4% of AML patients show MECOM rearrangements which serve as a biomarker for this subtype of AML that shows aggressive progression and poor prognosis and is distinctly defined under the 5th WHO Classification for hematologic malignancies.

description: The embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes (ETMR) is a rare, aggressive central nervous system (CNS) tumor that affects children younger than four years old. Approximately 90% of ETMRs harbor alterations in the miRNA cluster on chromosome 19q13.4 (C19MC), which is the largest miRNA cluster in the human genome. These alterations include focal amplification and gene fusions involving partner genes such as TTYH1 and, more rarely, MYO9B and MIRLET7BHG, leading to the upregulation of C19MC and contributing to ETMR tumorigenesis. Professional guidelines recognize C19MC alterations as essential for diagnosing C19MC-altered ETMR (WHO classification of tumor series, 5th edu.; vol 6).
name: AID169
summary: Alteration of chromosome 19 miRNA cluster (C19MC) is a primary diagnostic criterion for embryonal tumors with multilayered rosettes (ETMRs).

description: KMT2A rearrangements are detected in a subset of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients. KMT2A fusions in AML typically involve the N-terminal portion of KMT2A and the C-terminal portion of multiple different fusion partners. MLLT3 is the most common fusion partner. Professional guidelines (WHO) list KMT2A rearrangement as an essential diagnostic criteria and identification of the KMT2A fusion partner as a desirable diagnostic criterion for AML with KMT2A rearrangement (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

disease.name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With MLL Rearrangement

name: AID170
summary: KMT2A rearrangements are considered essential diagnostic criteria for acute myeloid leukemia with KMT2A rearrangement.

description: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP) and its variants, including the pigmented Bednar tumor, are defined by the presence of a COL1A1::PDGFB fusion, resulting from the translocation t(17;22)(q22;q13). This fusion consistently involves exon 2 of PDGFB and a variable breakpoint within exons 6-49 of COL1A1. Professional guidelines (WHO) list the detection of the COL1A1::PDGFB fusion as a diagnostic criterion for DFSP (WHO Classification of Tumours of Soft Tissue and Bone, 5th Edition).
name: AID171
summary: COL1A1-PDGFB fusion is a diagnostic criterion for dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP).

description: The myxoid liposarcoma (MLS, also known as MLPS) and its hypercellular round cell subtype are rare adipocyte-derived soft tissue sarcoma, accounting for 20-30% of liposarcoma. While this disease entity is more common in adults, it can affect individuals of any age and is the most prevalent liposarcoma subtype among children and adolescents. The molecular hallmark of this disease involves DDIT3 (CHOP, GADD153) translocations, with the t(12;16)(q13;p11)-driven FUS::DDIT3 fusions being more prevalent. The rare t(12;22)(q13;q12) translocation producing EWSR1::DDIT3 is found in 3% of cases. These adipocyte-specific chromosomal rearrangements contribute to MLS tumorigenesis by blocking normal adipocyte differentiation. Professional guidelines recognize DDIT3 rearrangement (FUS::DDIT3 or EWSR1::DDIT3 fusions) as desirable diagnostic criterion for MLS (WHO classification of tumor series, 5th ed.; vol 6; NCCN v1.2025).
name: AID179
summary: The t(12;16)(q13;p11) rearrangement generating FUS::DDIT3 fusion transcripts is a molecular diagnostic criterion for myxoid liposarcoma (MLS).

description: AR-V7 is an alternatively spliced version of the androgen receptor that was identified in LNCaP derivative cell lines which gained the ability to grow in an androgen depleted medium. The AR-V7 isoform consists of the first three exons of AR, along with a cryptic exon in place of exons 4 through 9. This isoform retains the N terminal transactivation domain, and the DNA binding domain of AR, but loses the hinge region and ligand binding domain, which suggests that this isoform has the capacity to transactivate downstream targets even in the absence of ligand. AR-V7 was expressed in androgen independent cell lines, and more frequently occurs in the setting of AR gene amplification. Expression of AR-V7 in androgen dependent cells induced androgen independence, and knockdown of AR-V7 in androgen independent cells inhibited androgen independent growth. AR-V7 shows increased capacity to translocate to the nucleus in an androgen independent manner. AR-V7 isoforms are found in castration-resistant prostate cancer, salivary duct carcinoma and breast carcinoma. AR-V7 is associated with resistance to Abiraterone and Enzalutamide in patients with metastatic prostate cancer.
name: AID180
summary: AR-V7 is associated with resistance to Abiraterone and Enzalutamide in patients with metastatic prostate cancer.

description: ZNF384 rearrangements are detected in a subset of B-lymphoblastic leukemia patients. ZNF384 fusions typically involve the N-terminal portion of partner genes fused to ZNF384's C-terminus, with TCF3 and EP300 being the most frequent partner genes. These fusions define a distinct subgroup characterized by weak CD10 and aberrant CD13/CD33 expression. Professional guidelines (WHO) list ZNF384 rearrangements as an essential diagnostic criterion for the subtype of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with ZNF384  rearrangement, within the category of B-ALL with other defined genetic alterations (WHO Classification of Tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

disease.name: B-lymphoblastic Leukaemia/lymphoma With Other Defined Genetic Alterations

name: AID181
summary: ZNF384 rearrangements are considered essential diagnostic criteria for B-ALL with other defined genetic alterations /B-ALL with ZNF384 rearrangements.

description: KMT2A rearrangements are detected in a subset of B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL) patients, especially infants. KMT2A fusions typically involve the N-terminal portion of KMT2A and the C-terminal portion of various fusion partners, with AFF1, MLLT1, and MLLT3 being most common. Professional guidelines (WHO and ICC) list KMT2A rearrangement as an essential diagnostic criterion for B-ALL with KMT2A rearrangement (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).
name: AID182
summary: KMT2A rearrangements are considered essential diagnostic criteria for B lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with KMT2A rearrangement.

description: NPM1 mutations are detected in a large subset of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients, particularly those with normal cytogenetics. These mutations typically consist of small insertions in the terminal coding exon of NPM1 (NM_002520.7 exon 11; historically refferd to as exon 12), resulting in elongation of the protein, disruption of the C-terminal nucleolar localization signal, and aberrant cytoplasmic localization (NPMc+). Professional guideline (WHO) recognize AML with mutated NPM1 as a distinct diagnostic entity, with the presence of an NPM1 mutation listed as an essential diagnostic criterion and FLT3 mutation status as a key prognostic determinant (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

disease.name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With Mutated NPM1

name: AID185
summary: NPM1 exon 11 mutation, resulting in disruption of the nucleolar localization signal and creation of a cytoplasmic localization signal, is a diagnostic criterion for a subtype of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with mutated NPM1.

description: CBFB::MYH11 is detected in a distinct subset of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients, historically classified as AML with inv(16)(p13q22) or t(16;16)(p13;q22). This rearrangement results in fusion of the CBFB gene on chromosome 16q22 with MYH11 on chromosome 16p13, producing the CBFB::MYH11 fusion transcript. Professional guidelines (WHO) recognize AML with CBFB::MYH11 as a distinct diagnostic entity, with the presence of the CBFB::MYH11 fusion serving as an essential diagnostic criterion (WHO classification of tumors' series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).

disease.name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia With Inv(16)(p13.1q22) Or T(16;16)(p13.1;q22)

name: AID186
summary: CBFB::MYH11 is considered an essential diagnostic criterion for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with CBFB::MYH11.

description: Myofibromas and myopericytomas harboring SRF gene fusions are a rare and diagnostically challenging entity that occurs mostly in children and young adults. SRF fusions typically involve the N-terminal portion of SRF and the C-terminal portion of various fusion partners, with RELA being the most common. Professional guidelines (WHO) list detection of SRF rearrangement as a diagnostic criterion for cellular cases of myofibroma (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).
name: AID187
summary: SRF rearrangement is a diagnostic criterion for myofibroma and myopericytoma.

description: Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML) is a well-defined myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by the t(9;22)(q34;q11.2) forming the  BCR::ABL1 fusion. The fusion is expressed from the derivative chromosome 22, known also as Philadelphia (Ph) chromosome. This fusion results in a constitutively active BCR::ABL1 tyrosine kinase, representing the initiating and defining molecular event in CML pathogenesis. Professional guidelines (WHO) list detection of BCR::ABL1 fusion as a diagnostic criterion for CML (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).
name: AID188
summary: BCR::ABL1 fusion is a diagnostic criterion for Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML).

description: B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL), BCR::ABL1 (Ph)-like subtype, is a high-risk leukemia occurring predominantly in adolescents and young adults (AYA). It is characterized by activation of cytokine receptor-like factor 2 (CRLF2) through either IGH::CRLF2 or P2RY8::CRLF2 gene fusions, resulting in CRLF2 overexpression. These rearrangements often co-occur with activating mutations in the JAK-STAT signaling pathway, most commonly JAK2. Professional guidelines (WHO) list detection of CRLF2 gene rearrangements or overexpression, often accompanied by JAK-STAT pathway alterations, as diagnostic criterion for B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL), BCR::ABL1 (Ph)-like (WHO classification of tumours series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).
name: AID189
summary: IGH::CRLF2 rearrangement resulting in CRLF2 overexpression, often accompanied by JAK-STAT pathway mutations, is a diagnostic criterion for B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (B-ALL), BCR::ABL1 (Ph)-like subtype.

description: Alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma (ARMS) is an aggressive soft tissue malignancy of children and adolescents that is defined by specific gene fusions, most commonly the PAX3::FOXO1. This fusion, resulting from a t(2;13)(q35;q14) translocation, is a primary molecular driver and a highly specific diagnostic marker for this tumor. Its detection is critical for distinguishing ARMS from histologic mimics, particularly the fusion-negative embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma. Professional guidelines (WHO) list the PAX3::FOXO1 fusion as a diagnostic criterion for alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma (WHO Classification of Tumours of Soft Tissue and Bone, 5th Edition).
name: AID190
summary: PAX3::FOXO1 fusion is a diagnostic criterion for alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma.

description: The round cell sarcoma (RCS) with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions is a rare undifferentiated sarcoma. It is characterized by gene fusion of a FET family gene EWSR1 or FUS joining with a downstream non-ETS family transcription factor such as NFATC2. The EWSR1::NFATC2 RCSs have a predilection for bones (mainly involved in the metaphysis or diaphysis of long bones) over soft tissue (4:1) with a strong male predominance (5:1). Together with FUS::NFATC2 RCSs, these tumors affect adolescents and adults with a median age of 32.3 years at presentation. The EWSR1::NFATC2 fusion typically results from an unbalanced translocation t(20;22)(q13;q12) and is amplified, which can be detected by EWSR1 break-apart FISH probes. Several fusion variants have been identified and may occur between exons 6-10 of EWSR1 and exons 3-4 of NFATC2. The resulting EWSR1::NFATC2 chimeric protein shows an uncontrolled nuclear localization and activation of NFATC2 to rewire the transcriptome and epigenome of the as yet identified cells of origin. Of significance, professional guidelines recognize ETMR1::NFATC2 gene fusions a diagnostic criterion for a subset of round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions (WHO classification of tumor series, 5th edu.; vol 6).

disease.name: Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion

name: AID191
summary: The t(20;22)(q13.2;q12.2) translocation generating the EWSR1::NFATC2 fusion transcript is a diagnostic criterion for a subset of (small) round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions.

description: PAX7::FOXO1 fusion–positive alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma represents a molecularly defined and diagnostically distinct subtype that predominantly affects children and young adults. The fusion event, which joins the DNA-binding domain of PAX7 with the transactivation domain of FOXO1, serves as the principal oncogenic driver. Professional guidelines (WHO) list the detection of PAX7::FOXO1 fusion as a diagnostic criterion for alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma (WHO Classification of Tumours, 5th Edition; Soft Tissue and Bone Tumours).
name: AID192
summary: PAX7::FOXO1 fusion is a diagnostic criterion for alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma.

description: Spindle cell and sclerosing rhabdomyosarcomas harboring MYOD1 p.L122R mutations are a distinct and often aggressive entity that occurs across pediatric and adult age groups. The MYOD1 p.L122R mutation is a recurrent hotspot mutation that serves as a primary oncogenic driver. In a study of 49 rhabdomyosarcoma cases, all 10 cases that were positive for L122R were either spindle cell or sclerosing subtypes of RMS (civic.EID:8193), and L122R is found at high frequencies in these subtypes (civic.EID:11582, civic.EID:11585). Professional guidelines (WHO) list the detection of MYOD1 mutation as a diagnostic criterion for spindle cell/sclerosing rhabdomyosarcoma (WHO Classification of Tumors, 5th Edition; Soft Tissue and Bone Tumors).
name: AID193
summary: MYOD1 p.L122R mutation is a diagnostic criterion for spindle cell/sclerosing rhabdomyosarcoma.

description: Synovial sarcomas harboring SS18::SSX1 gene fusions are a molecularly defined and diagnostically distinct entity that occurs across a wide age range and in various anatomical sites. The SS18::SSX1 fusion, resulting from the characteristic t(X;18) translocation, juxtaposes the N-terminal portion of SS18 with the C-terminal portion of SSX1 and is the most common fusion variant. Professional guidelines (WHO) list the detection of SS18::SSX1 fusion as a diagnostic criterion for synovial sarcoma (WHO Classification of Tumors, 5th Edition; Soft Tissue and Bone Tumors).
name: AID194
summary: SS18::SSX1 fusion is a diagnostic criterion for synovial sarcoma.

description: The round cell sarcoma (RCS) with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions is a rare undifferentiated sarcoma. It is characterized by gene fusion of a FET (FUS/EWS/TAF15, previously TET [FUS (TLS)/EWS/TAF15]) family gene EWSR1 or FUS joining with a downstream non-ETS family transcription factor such as NFATC2. The FUS-NFATC2 RCSs have been found exclusively in the long bones. Together with EWSR1-NFATC2 RCSs, these tumors have a strong male predominance (M:F, 5:1) and affect adolescents and adults with a median age of 32.3 years (aged 12-67 years) at presentation. The FUS::NFATC2 fusion results from the translocation t(16;20)(p11.2;q13.2) and has not shown amplification as EWSR1::NFATC2. Of significance, professional guidelines recognize FUS::NFATC2 gene fusions as a diagnostic criterion for a subset of round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions (WHO classification of tumor series, 5th ed.).

disease.name: Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion

name: AID197
summary: The t(16;20)(p11.2;q13.2) translocation generating the FUS::NFATC2 fusion transcript is a diagnostic criterion for a subset of (small) round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions.

description: RET M918T occurs in the kinase domain of RET, and is found in both germline and somatic RET mutations in medullary thyroid cancer (civic.EID:12711). M918T induces transformation of cells which are sensitive to treatment by selpercatinib (civic.EID:11867, civic.EID:11876). M918T is the most prevalent RET mutation found in patients enrolled in medullary thyroid cancer trials (civic.EID:8851, civic.EID:12708), and the only RET mutation reported in cancerhotspots V2. Patients with M918T have improved progression free survival when treated with selpercatinib over physician’s choice of vandetanib or cabozantinib (civic.EID:12598). Selpercatinib is approved for use in medullary thyroid cancer patients with RET mutations including M918T over 2 years of age based on the results of phase 1/2 (civic.EID:12056, civic.EID:12708) and LIBRETTO-531 phase 3 trials (civic.EID:12157).
name: AID200
summary: RET M918T is sensitive to selpercatinib in medullary thyroid cancer

description: Published sequencing studies have shown that RET mutations are very common in medullary thryoid carcinoma (MTC) and M918T is the most common specific variant, especially in the MEN2B clinical subtype of familial disease (civic.EID:78) but also in sporadic cases(civic.EID:12800). M918T mutations may predict worse outcomes (civic.EID:74). Biochemical and functional characterization demonstrates that the M918T mutation leads to functional activation of RET relative to wild-type through multiple complementary mechanisms, including increased ATP affinity (>10-fold) and complex stability, reduced conformational rigidity, and the promotion of ligand-independent dimerization and autophosphorylation (civic.EID:12805). Exogenous expression has been shown to induce transformation of Ba/F3 cells (civic.EID:11723), and drive colony formation in NIH3T3 cells (civic.EID:12709, OS2). RET M918T occurs in the region of the tyrosine kinase domain which is associated with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 B (OM1). RET M918T is predicted to be deleterious (CHASMplus score 0.314 > VECS gene-specific cutoff of 0.22, OP1). Eleven instances of the variant occur in cancerhotspots.org (V2): 6 Thyroid, 4 Adrenal Gland, 1 Breast (OP3). The variant is absent in gnomAD database (v4.1.0, OP4). Together these criteria indicate that M918T is likely oncogenic, with a score of 9.
name: AID202
summary: RET M918T is likely oncogenic in medullary thyroid cancer

description: FGFR1 Amplification is associated with poor clinical outcomes. In a large breast cancer cohort of 503 assessable patients, FGFR1 amplification was observed in 33 cases (6.6%) and was enriched in the more aggressive luminal B subtype, seen in 69.7 percent of amplified versus 32.6 percent in non-amplified tumors. In this study observed outcome differences did not achieve statistical significance, but there was a trend toward poorer distant metastasis-free survival in patients with FGFR1 amplification [HR=2.08; 95% CI 0.98 to 4.39, P=0.05) (civic.eid:12487). A similar association was observed in the H120 and METABRIC study cohorts of ER-positive breast cancer. In H210 FGFR1 amplification was observed in a higher percentage of luminal B (16.3%, N=17/103) vs luminal A (6.6%, N=6/92) cases and conferred a significant hazard ratio for relapse (HR = 1.96, 95% CI 1.031-3/72, P=0.038). In METABRIC (N=635) the percentage of cases with FGFR amplification was higher in luminal B than in luminal A cases (11.1% vs. 5.5%, P=0.001) and the median relapse-free survival was shorter for cases with amplification than for those without (12.2 vs 21.1 years) (civic.eid:12497). In a separate study of 100 metastatic breast cancer patients, FGFR1 amplification was found in 20 percent of the cohort and associated with decreased median overall survival of 32 versus 54 months (log-rank p=0.0018) (civic.eid:12532). A retrospective study of ctDNA samples from the PALOMA-3 trial (N=401) in patients with advanced ER+ breast cancer found that in both univariable and multivariable analyses gain of FGFR1 was associated with poorer progression-free survival in both treatment groups; there was no interaction with treatment randomization (civic.eid:12486).
name: AID203
summary: FGFR1 Amplification is associated with poor prognosis in breast cancer

description: VGLL2- and NCOA2-rearranged infantile spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma is a distinct and  prognostically favorable entity that occurs almost exclusively in infants under one year of age. VGLL2 or NCOA2 fusions occur with different partner genes, including TEAD1, SRF, and CITED2. Professional guidelines (WHO) list VGLL2 or NCOA2 rearrangements as a diagnostic criterion for the subtype of SCRMS (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).
name: AID205
summary: NCOA2 fusion is a diagnostic criterion for a subset of spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma (SCRMS).

description: Giant cell tumor of bone (GCT) is a locally aggressive and rarely metastasizing neoplasm, accounting for approximately 5% of all primary bone tumors. Driver mutations affecting H3F3A at codon p.G34—most commonly p.G34W (also reported as p.G35W)—are highly specific to GCT and are not observed in other bone tumors. These mutations are present in the majority of cases, reported in up to 92% and 96% of GCTs in different studies (civic.EID:6469, civic.EID:12749). H3F3A mutations are restricted to glycine 34 substitutions, with rare variants such as G34L, G34R, and G34M also described. While highly specific, sensitivity may vary depending on the detection method, with lower rates reported using Sanger sequencing (civic.EID:12750). The World Health Organization (WHO) classification of tumours recognizes the detection of H3F3A p.G34W as a diagnostic criterion for GCT (WHO Classification of Tumours, 5th edition, Volume 3: Soft Tissue and Bone Tumours).
name: AID206
summary: H3-3A G34W is a diagnostic criterion for bone giant cell tumor.

description: Gastroblastoma is a rare gastric tumor composed of epithelial and spindle cell components that occurs in both children and adults (civic.EID:12080, civic.EID:12753, civic.EID:12754, civic.EID:12755). Professional guidelines (WHO) list MALAT1::GLI1 fusion as a diagnostic criterium for gastroblastoma (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).
name: AID207
summary: MALAT1::GLI1 fusion is a diagnostic criterium for gastroblastoma.

description: The round cell sarcoma (RCS) with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions is a rare undifferentiated sarcoma. It is characterized by gene fusions involving a FET (FUS/EWS/TAF15, previously TET [FUS (TLS)/EWS/TAF15]) family gene (EWSR1 or FUS) joined with a downstream non-ETS family transcription factor such as PATZ1. The EWSR1::PATZ1 RCSs occur in the deep soft tissue with a predilection for thoracoabdominal regions and affect individuals with ages ranging from 1 to 81 years (mean of 42 years) at presentation. This gene fusion results from a cryptic paracentric inversion within chromosome 22q12.2, enabling co-directional transcription of EWSR1 and PATZ1 with variable breakpoints located within exons 7-9 of EWSR1 and exon 1 of PATZ1. The resulting chimeric protein joins the transcriptional activation domain of EWSR1 and the DNA-binding zinc fingers of PATZ1. Consequently, this rearrangement converts the transcriptional repressor PATZ1 to a transcriptional activator by the removal of its N-terminal transcriptional repressing BTB/POZ domain. Diagnostically, EWSR1::PATZ1 fusion can be identified by sequencing, but this rearrangement is not detectable by conventional karyotyping and is likely missed by FISH. Of significance, professional guidelines recognize EWSR1::PATZ1 gene fusions as a diagnostic criterion for a subset of round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions (WHO classification of tumor series, 5th ed.).

disease.name: Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion

name: AID208
summary: The cryptic intrachromosomal inversion within chromosome 22q12.2 generating the EWSR1::PATZ1 fusion transcript is a diagnostic criterion for a subset of (small) round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusions.

description: Pseudomyogenic hemangioendothelioma (PHE) is a rare endothelial tumor that predominantly affects children and young adults. The genetics of  PHE is not fully characterized. However, recent studies have identified SERPINE1::FOSB (civic.eid:11785), WWTR1::FOSB (civic.eid:12752), and ACTB::FOSB (civic.eid:12779) fusions that support the diagnosis of PHE. The World Health Organization (WHO) classification of tumours recognizes the detection of FOSB fusions as a diagnostic criterion for PHE (WHO Classification of Tumours, 5th edition, Volume 3: Soft Tissue and Bone Tumours).
name: AID212
summary: FOSB fusions  are a diagnostic criterion for Pseudomyogenic Hemangioendothelioma.

description: TYK2 gene rearrangements are a rare, recurrent, and diagnostic finding in B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma subtype with BCR::ABL1-like features. These fusions juxtapose a partner gene's (commonly MYB) N-terminus with the C-terminal tyrosine kinase domain of TYK2, leading to its constitutive, oncogenic activation. Professional guidelines (WHO) list TYK2 rearrangements as a diagnostic criterion for B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with BCR::ABL1-like features (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).
name: AID213
summary: TYK2 rearrangements are considered diagnostic criterion for B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with BCR::ABL1-like features.

description: LYN gene rearrangements are a rare, recurrent, and diagnostic finding in the B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma subtype with BCR::ABL1-like features. These fusions juxtapose a partner gene's (commonly NCOR1) N-terminus with the C-terminal tyrosine kinase domain of LYN, leading to its constitutive, oncogenic activation (civic.eid:12801, civic.eid:12802, civic.eid:12809). Professional guidelines (WHO) list rearrangements involving kinase genes—including LYN— as a diagnostic criterion for B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma with BCR::ABL1-like features (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).
name: AID214
summary: LYN rearrangements are considered diagnostic criteria for B-lymphoblastic Leukemia/lymphoma With BCR::ABL1-like Features.

description: Spindle cell/sclerosing rhabdomyosarcoma (SCSRMS) is a rare type of rhabdomyosarcoma characterized by fascicular spindle cell and/or sclerosing morphology. Three subtypes are recognized: congenital/infantile SCSRMS, which typically affects patients under 12 years and is associated with VGLL2, NCOA2, or CITED2 gene fusions; MYOD1-mutant SCSRMS, which is more aggressive and shows a decreased male-to-female ratio; and intraosseous SCSRMS, defined by EWSR1 or FUS fused to TFCP2, which primarily arises in bone in adolescents and young adults (civic.eid:12825, civic.eid:12826, civic.eid:12827). The intraosseous subtype often displays variable spindle and epithelioid morphology and may show cytokeratin or ALK positivity in a subset of tumors. Clinically, intraosseous SCSRMS typically presents as a rapidly growing, painless mass with aggressive behavior and frequent metastases. Detection of the EWSR1::TFCP2 gene fusion by FISH or targeted RNA sequencing serves as a key molecular diagnostic criterion for this subtype (civic.eid:12825, civic.eid:12826, civic.eid:12827). Professional guidelines list these gene rearrangements and fusions as a diagnostic criterion for intraosseous SCSRMS (WHO classification of tumor series, 5th ed. volume 3).
name: AID217
summary: EWSR1::TFCP2 gene fusion is a diagnostic criterion for intraosseous spindle cell/sclerosing rhabdomyosarcoma (SCSRMS).

description: Clear cell sarcoma (CCS) is a malignant mesenchymal tumor of the deep soft tissue found typically in the lower extremities of young adults (civic.eid:12829). Cytogenetic studies have shown that CCS often has a recurrent chromosomal translocation: t(12;22)(q13;q12) (civic.eid:12829, civic.eid:12830, civic.eid:8265). Further, reverse transcriptase (RT)-PCR performed on RNA from fresh, frozen, or FFPE tumor tissue confirms the presence of an in-frame gene fusion between Exon 8 of EWSR1 and codon 65 of ATF1 (civic.eid:12830). This RT-PCR assay can be used as a molecular diagnostic test for CCS. The World Health Organization (WHO) classification of tumors recognizes the detection of EWSR1::ATF1 as a diagnostic criterion for CCS (WHO Classification of Tumors, 5th edition, Volume 3: Soft Tissue and Bone Tumors).
name: AID219
summary: EWSR1::ATF1 in-frame gene fusion is a diagnostic criterion for clear cell sarcoma (CCS)

description: Osteoblastoma and osteoid osteoma are benign bone tumors that predominantly affect adolescents and young adults. Whole-genome sequencing and cytogenetic studies have shown that these tumors are characterized by FOS rearrangements in the majority of cases, with FOSB rearrangements present in a smaller subset (civic.eid:11596, civic.eid:11597, civic.eid:11787). The rearrangements typically retain the 5' end of FOS or FOSB, including the dominant transactivation and bZIP domains, and involve various 3' fusion partners such as ANKH, RUNX2, and others (civic.eid:11596, civic.eid:11787). FOS immunohistochemistry shows strong nuclear expression in nearly all tumors with FOS rearrangements, and FISH can confirm these genetic alterations, aiding in differentiation from more aggressive osteoblastic osteosarcomas (civic.eid:11596, civic.eid:11786, civic.eid:11597). Professional guidelines (WHO) list a FOS or FOSB rearrangement as a diagnostic criterion for osteoblastoma and osteoid osteoma (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 7).
name: AID222
summary: A FOS or FOSB rearrangement is a diagnostic criterion for osteoblastoma and osteoid osteoma.

description: The EWSR1::CREB1 fusion represents the defining molecular feature of angiomatoid fibrous histiocytoma (AFH), supported by multi‑platform evidence demonstrating consistent detection of the canonical EWSR1 exon 7–CREB1 exon 7 fusion across cohorts (civic.EID :12855). This fusion aids in distinguishing AFH from clear cell sarcoma and other EWSR1‑rearranged mimics (civic.EID:12852). Although most EWSR1::CREB1‑positive AFH tumors show indolent clinical behavior, a documented case of widely metastatic, fatal disease confirms that this fusion, while diagnostically definitive, does not uniformly confer a favorable prognosis (civic.EID:12853). The World Health Organization (WHO) classification of tumors recognizes the detection of EWSR1::CREB1 as a diagnostic criterion for AFH (WHO Classification of Tumors, 5th edition, Volume 3: Soft Tissue and Bone Tumors).
name: AID223
summary: The EWSR1::CREB1 fusion represents the defining molecular feature of angiomatoid fibrous histiocytoma (AFH).

description: B-lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) with PAX5 alterations (PAX5Alt) is a recently described subtype classified within B-ALL/lymphoma (B-ALL/LBL) with other defined genetic alterations (civic.EID:12867, civic.EID:12869). PAX5 is a B-lineage–specific transcription factor and a master regulator of B-cell development. A variety of PAX5 alterations have been identified in PAX5Alt B-ALL, including PAX5 fusions with different partner genes (excluding PAX5::JAK2 and PAX5::ZCCHC7), non–p.P80R point mutations, and focal intragenic amplifications (civic.EID:12867). More than two dozen translocation partners have been reported, all producing in-frame fusion proteins, with PAX5::ETV6 being the most frequently described (civic.EID:12867, civic.EID:12869). Professional guidelines list the presence of PAX5 fusions (except PAX5::JAK2 and PAX5::ZCCHC7) as a diagnostic criterion for PAX5Alt B-ALL (WHO Classification of Tumours Series, 5th edition, Vol. 11).
name: AID227
summary: PAX5 fusions with different partner genes, excluding PAX5::JAK2 and PAX5::ZCCHC7, represent a diagnostic criterion for B-lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) with PAX5 alterations (PAX5alt).

description: Infantile spindle cell and sclerosing rhabdomyosarcoma (SCSRMS) is a rare subtype of rhabdomyosarcoma that occurs in children under one year of age (civic.eid:12870, civic.eid:11565, civic.eid:11568, civic.eid:12871). While histopathologic analysis identifies a monomorphic spindle cell pattern resembling infantile fibrosarcoma in these tumors (civic.eid:11565, civic.eid:11568), molecular studies confirm recurrent VGLL2 fusions, most commonly VGLL2::NCOA2 and VGLL2::CITED2 (civic.eid:12870, civic.eid:11565, civic.eid:11568, civic.eid:12871). These fusions can be detected using RNA sequencing, FISH, targeted DNA sequencing, or RT-PCR, and serve as a molecular diagnostic test for infantile SCSRMS (civic.eid:12870, civic.eid:11565, civic.eid:11568, civic.eid:12871). The presence of VGLL2 fusions defines a distinct, clinically favorable infantile SCSRMS subgroup and enables molecular distinction from embryonal and alveolar RMS subtypes (civic.eid:12870, civic.eid:11565, civic.eid:11568, civic.eid:12871). Professional guidelines (WHO) list VGLL2 rearrangements as a diagnostic criterion for the subtype of SCSRMS (WHO classification of tumors series, 5th ed.; vol. 11).
name: AID228
summary: VGLL2 fusion is a diagnostic criterion for a subset of spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma (SCRMS).

description: HRAS G13R causes increased proliferation (civic.EID:12906, OS2), increased pERK/ERK ratio and increased GTP-bound HRAS (civic.EID:12905, OS2). This variant count in cancerhotspots.org (V2) is 22 with  50 samples with a somatic variant at the same amino acid position (OS3). The variant is absent in gnomAD database (v4.1.0, OP4). Both OS2 and OS3 criteria are satisfied at full strength (OP1). Together these criteria indicate that G13R is oncogenic, with a score of 10. Variant classification is done using ClinGen MAPK/ERK pathway sc-VCEP guidelines.
name: AID233
summary: HRAS G13R (NM_005343.4:c.37G>C) is oncogenic

description: Myoepithelial tumors arising outside the salivary glands are biologically distinct from their salivary gland counterparts. They can occur in a wide range of deep and superficial soft tissue sites, as well as in bone and the skin (civic.EID:12926). EWSR1 rearrangements are identified in approximately 45% of cases and are particularly enriched in pediatric and young adult patients (civic.EID:12926). Multiple fusion partners have been reported, including POU5F1, PBX1, ZNF444, KLF15, ATF1, and KLF17, contributing to the notable histologic and biologic heterogeneity observed across cases (civic.EID:12927). Histologic patterns are variable, encompassing epithelioid, spindle, clear cell, and small round cell morphologies, and tumors may show benign or malignant behavior (civic.EID:12929). Rare fusions, such as EWSR1::KLF15 and EWSR1::ZNF444, highlight the importance of integrating molecular testing with morphology and immunohistochemistry to accurately classify these tumors and inform prognosis (civic.EID:12930). Professional guidelines list the presence of EWSR1 rearrangements as a diagnostic criterion for myoepithelial tumors of soft tissue (civic.EID:12931).
name: AID243
summary: EWSR1 fusions with various partner genes, including POU5F1, PBX1, ZNF444, KLF15, ATF1, and KLF17, represent a diagnostic criterion for myoepithelial tumors of soft tissue.

description: MAP2K1 P124S causes increased colony formation and increased pERK/ERK ratio (civic.eid:12986, OS2). In cancerhotspots.org there are more than 10 (15) samples with the same amino acid change and less than 50 (25) samples with a somatic variant at the same amino acid position (OM3). The variant is absent in gnomAD database (v4.1.0) (OP4). Together these criteria indicate that P124S is likely oncogenic, with a score of 7. Variant classification was done using ClinGen Somatic MAPK/ERK pathway SC-VCEP guidelines.
name: AID251
summary: MAP2K1 p.P124S (NM_002755.3:c.370C>T) is likely oncogenic.

name: AID252
summary: The variant p.Ser214Phe (NM_001654.5:c.641C>T ; CA16602805 ) in the ARAF gene was classified as  Likely Oncogenic  in  malignant neoplasms by the ClinGen MAPK/ERK Pathway SC-VCEP

description: The variant p.Ser257Leu (NM_002880.4:c.770C>T ; CA235334 ) in the RAF1 (CRAF) gene was classified as  Likely Oncogenic  in  malignant neoplasms by the ClinGen MAPK/ERK Pathway SC-VCEP, using SC-VCEP Specifications created in 2026. This variant satisfies the following criteria: OS2, functional evidence PMID: 24569458, increased colony formation, increased pMEK/MEK ratio; PMID: 38127827, increased pERK/ERK ratio; OM1, variant in exon 7 (AA 227-278); OP4, absent in controls, no entry in gnomAD. This results in 1 Strong, 1 moderate AND 1 supporting evidence codes and a total of 7 points. Additional notes on this curation record are as follows: The count in cancerhotspots.org is 24 (25 samples with a somatic variant at the same amino acid position); relevant tumor type(s): neoplasms.
name: AID253
summary: The variant p.Ser257Leu (NM_002880.4:c.770C>T ; CA235334 ) in the RAF1 (CRAF) gene was classified as  Likely Oncogenic in malignant neoplasms by the ClinGen MAPK/ERK Pathway SC-VCEP.

description: The ERBB2 G292R variant is a rare variant that has been observed in cancers of the hepatobiliary and urinary tracts; it is not prevalent in breast cancer. This variant is located in the extracellular cysteine-rich domain C1 that is critical for dimerization (civic.EID:12118) (OM1). Functional data from in vitro assays of cell growth and focus formation are limited, and results have been mixed (civic.EID:12116, civic.EID:12117, civic.EID:12118)(OS2_Moderate). CHASMplus scores do not indicate that this is a deleterious mutation (scores between 0.377-0.567 do not reach the VECS gene-specific cutoff of 0.68 for ERBB2). No instances are reported in cancerhotspots (V2). The variant is absent in the gnomAD database (v4.1.0, OP4). In the absence of  stronger functional data, these criteria indicate that G292R remains a Variant of Unknown Significance (VUS), with a score of 5.
name: AID277
summary: The ERBB2 variant G292R is of uncertain significance.

description: The ERBB2 V777L variant is found in breast cancer and at low frequency in other solid tumors; it may or may not be associated with gene amplification (civic.EID:12103). It displays greater tyrosine kinase activity than wild-type in multiple in vitro kinase assays (civic.EID:12103). It induces anchorage-independent growth and tumor formation in xenografts when stably over-expressed in cultured murine NCI-H508 colon cancer cells (civic.EID:4452) NIH-3T3 cells and MCF10A human breast epithelial cells (civic.EID:12103, civic.EID:12104 (OS2). This variant is located in the ATP-binding site of the tyrosine kinase catalytic domain (OM1). ERBB2 V777L is predicted to be deleterious (CHASMplus scores between 0.761-0.803 exceed the VECS gene-specific cutoff of 0.68 for ERBB2, OP1). Seventeen instances of the variant occur in cancerhotspots.org (V2), 6 in breast, 4 in colon, and 7 in other cancer types (OP3). The variant is absent in the gnomAD database (v4.1.0, OP4). Together these criteria indicate that V777L is likely oncogenic, with a score of 9.

description: The H3C2 K28M  (K27M) mutation has the same amino acid change as an established oncogenic variant at the canonical hotspot for histone mutant glioma (OS1, 4 points). H3C2 K27M variant causes a global reduction in H3K27me3 compared to non-K27M tumors (civic EID: 131177). Functional studies demonstrated that the homologous H3.1 K27M variant causes a global reduction in H3K27me3 through dominant negative mechanism of inhibition of PRC2, establishing a biologically relevant oncogenic mechanism applicable to H3C2 K27M (civic.EID:13177) (OS2, 4 points). The affected lysine 27 residue represents a recurrent somatic hotspot in more than 20 reported tumors harboring pathogenic variants at this amino acid position (OS3). It has been documented in the diffuse midline glioma (OP2). This variant is not known as a recurrent germline variant and is not reported as a population polymorphism. (OP4). The listed evidence indicates the H3 variant to be oncogenic utilizing the ClinGen Histone H3 Somatic Cancer Variant Curation Expert Panel criteria (OS1+OS2+OS3+OP2+OP4).
